rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: One reading takes morning and evening remembrance as the five prayers: dawn, noon and afternoon, sunset and night; the long night glorification is night vigil.
rows.anchor: البكرة هي صلاة الصبح والأصيل صلاة الظهر والعصر

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some held that night vigil was obligatory for the Prophet and later abrogated, reasoning that the repeated imperative expresses obligation.
rows.anchor: كان ذلك من الواجبات على الرسول عليه السلام

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Others held that the night vigil is voluntary and its ruling remains in force.
rows.anchor: بل المراد التطوع وحكمه ثابت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second reading takes the command as verbal and inward praise, requiring remembrance of God by heart and tongue at all times, as in 33:41-42.
rows.anchor: ذاكرا لله في جميع الأوقات ليلا ونهارا بقلبه ولسانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the gift of revelation and guidance, the Prophet is told to obey God alone; knowing divine names and attributes is possible, but created minds cannot reach the divine essence.
rows.anchor: العقول البشرية ليس عندها إلا معرفة الأسماء والصفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seven heavens are strongly and expertly made, unaffected by time and without fissures; 21:32 similarly calls heaven a protected roof.
rows.anchor: محكمة قوية الخلق لا يؤثر فيها مرور الزمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the heavens a structure rather than merely a roof stresses that, despite being above us, they are as resistant to collapse as a building.
rows.anchor: فالغرض من اختيار هذا اللفظ هذه الدقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thajj can be intransitive, meaning to flow, or transitive, meaning to pour; the hadith pairs loud talbiya with pouring sacrificial blood.
rows.anchor: أفضل الحج العج والثج أي رفع الصوت بالتلبية وصب دماء الهدي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas was called thajjaj because he poured forth abundant speech in his sermons.
rows.anchor: وكان ابن عباس مثجا أي يثج الكلام ثجا في خطبته

rows.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل وقتادة
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi, Muqatil and Qatada explain thajjaj as water flowing in a continuous, abundant stream.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي ومقاتل وقتادة الثجاج ههنا المتدفق المنصب

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj glosses thajjaj as pouring, as though the water pours itself; the point is repeated rain and abundant benefit.
rows.anchor: معناه الصباب كأنه يثج نفسه أي يصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All terrestrial growth falls into three exhaustive classes: grain with husks, grasses without husks or stems, and trees that form gardens; 20:54 names the first two.
rows.anchor: فثبت بالدليل العقلي انحصار ما ينبت في الأرض في هذه الأقسام الثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grain comes first because it is basic food, plants next because animals need them, and orchards last because fruit is less essential.
rows.anchor: وإنما قدم الله تعالى الحب لأنه هو الأصل في الغذاء

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says alfaf has no singular, like awzaʿ and akhyaf.
rows.anchor: ذكر صاحب الكشاف أنه لا واحد له كالأوزاع والأخياف

rows.speaker: الأخفش والكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash and al-Kisaʾi give the singular as lif with kasra; al-Kisaʾi also allows lif with damma.
rows.anchor: فقال الأخفش والكسائي واحدها لف بالكسر

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad rejects the damma form and instead proposes lifa as singular, pluralized as lif and then alfaf.
rows.anchor: وأنكر المبرد الضم ، وقال بل واحدها لفاء وجمعها لف ، وجمع لف ألفاف

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffal offers lifif as a possible singular, by analogy with sharif and ashraf; alfaf means closely interwoven gardens.
rows.anchor: وقيل : يحتمل أن يكون جمع لفيف كشريف وأشرف نقله القفال رحمه الله

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad tentatively connects tamma to a horse exhausting itself in a run or water filling an entire river.
rows.anchor: قال المبرد : أخذت فيما أحسب من قولهم : طم الفرس طميما

rows.speaker: الليث
rows.claim: Al-Layth derives the root from filling a well with earth and burying it, and from a flood that covers a cistern.
rows.anchor: وقال الليث : الطم طم البئر بالتراب ، وهو الكبس

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffal says the root means burying and rising over; tamma is any great calamity that overwhelms and eclipses everything before it.
rows.anchor: قال القفال : أصل الطم الدفن والعلو ، وكل ما غلب شيئا وقهره وأخفاه فقد طمه

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some identify the great catastrophe with Resurrection, whose fire, terrifying assembly and extraordinary signs eclipse every earlier terror.
rows.anchor: إنها يوم القيامة لأنه يشاهد فيه من النار

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan identifies it as the second blast, when all creatures are gathered for the Resurrection assembly.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن : إنها هي النفخة الثانية التي عندها تحشر الخلائق إلى موقف القيامة

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Others identify the catastrophe with the time described by the next verses: perhaps the reading of each person's record, or the dispatch of people to Paradise and Hell.
rows.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون ذلك الوقت وقت قراءة الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On seeing deeds recorded in the book, people recall actions they had forgotten, as 58:6 says God counted them while they forgot.
rows.anchor: يعني إذا رأى أعماله مدونة في كتابه تذكرها ، وكان قد نسيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means Hell is plainly exposed to every viewer; one interpretation is figurative visibility, which does not require every person to see it.
rows.anchor: أنها تظهر إظهارا مكشوفا لكل ناظر ذي بصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, everyone with sight, believers and unbelievers alike, sees Hell; it is the disbelievers' home, while believers cross it, supported by 19:71-72.
rows.anchor: وهذا يفيد أن كل الناس يرونها من المؤمنين والكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no conflict with 26:90-91, which says Hell is exposed to the deviators, because believers see it while passing and deviators reach it as their destination.
rows.anchor: ولا منافاة بين الأمرين

rows.speaker: أبو نهيك
rows.claim: Abu Nuhayk reads the verb as barrazat, with a different vocalization.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو نهيك { وبرزت }

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reads liman raʾā, 'for whoever saw.'
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود : لمن رأى

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima reads liman tarā, making Hell the subject, as in 25:12; another construal addresses Muhammad about his persecutors.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عكرمة : لمن ترى ، والضمير للجحيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing Resurrection generally, God divides those morally responsible into wretched and blessed, beginning with the wretched.
rows.anchor: قسم المكلفين قسمين : الأشقياء والسعداء ، فذكر حال الأشقياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear of one's Lord counters transgression, while restraining desire counters preferring worldly life; fear depends on knowledge (35:28) and causes restraint, so cause precedes effect.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الخوف من الله هو السبب المعين لدفع الهوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two descriptions encompass all virtues, just as the paired descriptions of Hell's people encompass all vices.
rows.anchor: وكما دخل في ذينك الصفتين جميع القبائح

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A reported occasion links the verses to Abu Aziz ibn Umayr and Musab ibn Umayr: Musab killed his brother at Uhud and shielded the Prophet until pierced by spears.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الآيتان نزلتا في أبي عزيز بن عمير ومصعب بن عمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After proving Resurrection possible, affirming it, and describing its general and moral states, the passage turns to the question of its timing.
rows.anchor: واعلم أنه تعالى لما بين بالبرهان العقلي إمكان القيامة ، ثم أخبر عن وقوعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists may ask sarcastically to make followers think Resurrection baseless, or impatiently demand its time, as in 42:18.
rows.anchor: فقالوا على سبيل الاستهزاء : { أيان مرساها }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mursa may mean when God establishes and brings the Hour into being, or its endpoint and resting place, like a ship's mooring.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : متى إرساؤها ، أي إقامتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading asks why the Prophet is occupied with remembering and disclosing its appointed time; Aisha reports that he kept mentioning and being asked about the Hour until this verse came down.
rows.anchor: وعن عائشة ( لم يزل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يذكر الساعة ويسأل عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading rebukes the question itself: the Prophet, final messenger, has given signs of the Hour's nearness, enough to prepare people, while its knowledge belongs to God alone.
rows.anchor: أرسلك وأنت خاتم الأنبياء وآخر الرسل ذاكرا من أنواع علاماتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's task is warning, which does not require knowing the Hour's time; warning is more effective when its time is unknown.
rows.anchor: بأن الإنذار والتخويف إنما يتمان إذا لم يكن العلم بوقت قيام القيامة حاصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet warns everyone, but those who fear the Hour are specified because they benefit from warning.
rows.anchor: أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام منذر للكل إلا أنه خص بمن يخشى

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says mundhir is normally indefinite with tanwin for present or future action because it stands for a verb; tanwin may be dropped for lightness, while past use requires annexation.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : مفعل وفاعل إذا كان كل واحد منهما لمايستقبل أو للحال ينون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When they see what was promised, worldly life will seem to have lasted only an hour, as in 46:35.
rows.anchor: كأنهم لم يلبثوا في الدنيا إلا ساعة من نهار

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Ata, says the final pronoun in duhaha is an additive particle: they stayed only an evening or a morning.
rows.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس : الهاء والألف صلة للكلام

rows.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Farra and al-Zajjaj understand 'its morning' as the morning of the day whose evening is named; Arabic can say 'evening or its morning.'
rows.anchor: قال الفراء والزجاج : المراد بإضافة الضحى إلى العشية إضافتها إلى يوم العشية

rows.speaker: النحويون
rows.claim: The grammarians allow an annexation based on the slightest relation: an earlier morning may be called the morning of its later evening; the ordeal is called evening and relief its morning.
rows.anchor: يكفي في حسن الإضافة أدنى سبب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interpretation of the oath as stars fits better than wild cattle, and stars are nobler objects for an oath.
rows.anchor: محل قسم الله كلما كان أعظم وأعلى رتبة كان أولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khunnas is the plural of khanis; khunas with light pronunciation can be the plural of khansa or akhnas, while for wild cattle it can mean hiding in a lair.
rows.anchor: أن ( الخنس ) جمع خانس من الخنوس

rows.speaker: أهل اللغة
rows.claim: Arabic lexicographers say asʿasa is a contronym: the night may be said to asʿasa when it begins or when it ends.
rows.anchor: ذكر أهل اللغة أن عسعس من الأضداد

rows.speaker: العجاج
rows.claim: Al-Ajjaj's verse uses asʿasa for night retreating as dawn breathes and the night departs.
rows.anchor: وانجاب عنها ليلها وعسعسا

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda cites a line using asʿasa for night arriving.
rows.anchor: وأنشد أبو عبيدة في معنى أقبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some take asʿasa as the night coming on, paired with dawn's arrival; others take it as night retreating at the first light, followed by dawn becoming fully bright, like 74:33-34.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من قال : بل المراد أدبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dawn's breathing means that it brightens, as in 74:34.
rows.anchor: وأما قوله تعالى : { والصبح إذا تنفس } أي إذا أسفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One metaphor gives dawn a spirit and breeze as it arrives; another compares dark night to a grief-stricken person relieved by taking a breath when dawn comes.
rows.anchor: فإذا تنفس وجد راحة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the oath is by ordinary dawn, true and false, whose light ends night, spreads people and animals in search of provision, and offers an image of resurrection.
rows.anchor: ما روي عن ابن عباس أن الفجر هو الصبح المعروف ، فهو انفجار الصبح الصادق والكاذب

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some take dawn as the whole day, with its beginning naming the whole, as in oaths by forenoon and daybreak of day.
rows.anchor: المراد به جميع النهار إلا أنه دل بالابتداء على الجميع

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Others take it as the Fajr prayer, when night and day angels gather to hear its recitation.
rows.anchor: المراد نفسه صلاة الفجر وإنما أقسم بصلاة الفجر

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: One specific dawn is Eid al-Adha, when Abrahamic rites and sacrifice occur; the pilgrim's offering recalls the substitute sacrifice in 37:107.
rows.anchor: أنه فجر يوم النحر ، وذلك لأن أمر المناسك من خصائص ملة إبراهيم

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Another is dawn of Dhu al-Hijja, paired with the ten nights because the month begins this great pilgrimage worship.
rows.anchor: أراد فجر ذي الحجة لأنه قرن به قوله : { وليال عشر }

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Another is dawn of Muharram, the year's first day, associated with recurring yearly rites; a report calls Muharram God's greatest month and Ibn Abbas calls it the year's dawn.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أنه قال : فجر السنة هو المحرم

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: A further interpretation is springs of water, whose flowing sustains life.
rows.anchor: أنه عنى بالفجر العيون التي تنفجر منها المياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ten nights are indefinite because they have exceptional virtues, and the indefinite form signals their great distinction.
rows.anchor: إنما جاءت منكرة من بين ما أقسم الله به لأنها ليال مخصوصة بفضائل

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: One interpretation is the first ten days of Dhu al-Hijja, devoted to pilgrimage rites; a report says righteous deeds in these days are especially excellent.
rows.anchor: أنها عشر ذي الحجة لأنها أيام الاشتغال بهذا النسك

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Another interpretation is all ten days of Muharram, including the honored day of Ashura and the merit of fasting it.
rows.anchor: أنها عشر المحرم من أوله إلى آخره

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: A third interpretation is Ramadan's last ten nights, containing the Night of Decree; a report urges seeking it then, and the Prophet used to devote himself and awaken his family.
rows.anchor: أنها العشر الأواخر من شهر رمضان ، أقسم الله تعالى بها لشرفها

rows.speaker: يونس
rows.claim: Shaf and witr mean even and odd; Yunus says people of the highlands pronounce witr with fatḥa for number and kasra for vengeance, while Tamim uses kasra for both.
rows.anchor: أهل العالية يقولون الوتر بالفتح في العدد

rows.speaker: الحسن والأعمش وابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Hasan, al-Aʿmash and Ibn Abbas read witr with kasra; the people of Medina read it with fatḥa, a Hijazi form.
rows.anchor: والكسر قراءة الحسن والأعمش وابن عباس

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: One interpretation makes even the Day of Sacrifice and odd the Day of Arafat: Arafat is central to pilgrimage, while sacrifice and major rites occur on the former.
rows.anchor: أن الشفع يوم النحر والوتر يوم عرفة

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Another makes even and odd the days of tashriq: the two days after sacrifice and the third, as 2:203 says; proponents prefer this because it avoids reusing days in the ten nights and covers the rites.
rows.anchor: الشفع هو يومان بعد يوم النحر ، الوتر هو اليوم الثالث

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: A third account makes Adam paired with his wife and God the One; another makes Adam and Eve the pair and God the odd.
rows.anchor: الوتر آدم شفع بزوجته

rows.speaker: عمران بن الحصين عن النبي
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet through Imran ibn Husayn identifies paired and odd prayers; prayer follows faith and has high devotional rank.
rows.anchor: روى عمران بن الحصين عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : ( هي الصلوات

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Even means all creation, since 51:49 and 78:8 say things and people were created in pairs; odd means God.
rows.anchor: الشفع هو الخلق كله لقوله تعالى : { ومن كل شيء خلقنا زوجين }

rows.speaker: بعض المتكلمين
rows.claim: Some theologians reject identifying God as the odd alongside created pairs: the implied oath is by their Lord, God is not named alongside another in this way, and the report 'God is odd and loves odd' is not firmly established.
rows.anchor: لا يصح أن يقال الوتر هو الله لوجوه

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Another interpretation includes every created thing, each of which is either paired or odd, under an oath by the Lord of both, as in 69:38-39.
rows.anchor: أن شيئا من المخلوقات لا ينفك عن كونه شفعا ووترا

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Even is the eight ranks of Paradise and odd the seven levels of Hell.
rows.anchor: الشفع درجات الجنة وهي ثمانية ، والوتر دركات النار وهي سبعة

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Even denotes paired created attributes such as knowledge and ignorance or life and death, while odd denotes God's attributes without opposites.
rows.anchor: الشفع صفات الخلق كالعلم والجهل والقدرة والعجز والإرادة والكراهية والحياة والموت

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Even and odd may denote numbers, the indispensable means of reckoning, writing and setting worship times, linked to 96:4-5, 55:4-5 and 10:5.
rows.anchor: المراد بالشفع والوتر ، نفس العدد فكأنه أقسم بالحساب

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says even means days and nights, and odd is the Resurrection Day after which no night comes.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل الشفع هو الأيام والليالي والوتر هو اليوم الذي لا ليل بعده وهو يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Even denotes prophets with two names, such as Muhammad and Ahmad, while odd denotes prophets with one name, such as Adam and Noah.
rows.anchor: الشفع كل نبي له اسمان مثل محمد وأحمد والمسيح وعيسى ويونس وذي النون

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Another account makes Adam and Eve the pair and Mary the odd.
rows.anchor: الشفع آدم وحواء والوتر مريم

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Even refers to Moses' twelve springs and odd to his nine signs, as listed in 17:101.
rows.anchor: الشفع العيون الإثنتا عشرة ، التي فجرها الله تعالى لموسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Even means the days of Aad and odd their nights, in connection with 69:7's seven nights and eight days.
rows.anchor: الشفع أيام عاد والوتر لياليهم لقوله تعالى : { سبع ليال وثمانية أيام حسوما }

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Even denotes the twelve constellations and odd the seven planets, linked to 25:61.
rows.anchor: الشفع البروج الإثنا عشر لقوله

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Even and odd may mean a month of thirty days and one of twenty-nine.
rows.anchor: الشفع الشهر الذي يتم ثلاثين يوما ، والوتر الشهر الذي يتم تسعة وعشرين يوما

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Even is the body's paired members and odd the heart, since a person has one heart, as in 33:4.
rows.anchor: الشفع الأعضاء والوتر القلب ، قال تعالى : { ما جعل الله لرجل من قلبين في جوفه }

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Even denotes the two lips and odd the tongue, as in 90:9.
rows.anchor: الشفع الشفتان / والوتر اللسان قال تعالى : { ولسانا وشفتين }

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Even means the two prostrations and odd the bowing in prayer.
rows.anchor: الشفع السجدتان والوتر الركوع

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Even means the eight gates of Paradise and odd the seven gates of Hell.
rows.anchor: الشفع أبواب الجنة لأنها ثمانية والوتر أبواب النار لأنها سبعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says the oath refers generally to two noble things; no listed interpretation is fixed by the wording unless a Prophetic report or interpretive consensus establishes it, though the article may support a universal reading.
rows.anchor: والظاهر لا إشعار له بشيء من هذه الأشياء على التعيين ، فإن ثبت في شيء منها خبر عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أو إجماع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yasri can mean the night passes, like 74:33 and 81:17, or can mean traveling through the night; Qatada takes it as night arriving.
rows.anchor: المسألة الأولى : { إذا يسر } إذا يمضي كما قال : { واليل إذا * أدبر }

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most exegetes take the verse as the night in general: alternating night and day is a great divine benefit and evidence of a wise, knowing governor.
rows.anchor: أكثر المفسرين على أنه ليس المراد منه ليلة مخصوصة بل العموم

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil identifies the night as the night at Muzdalifa, when pilgrims travel; the Prophet sent weaker family members ahead, and Shafiʿi permits this after midnight.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل : هلي ليلة المزدلفة فقوله : { إذا يسر } أي إذا يسار فيه

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says a reading retains the final ya; he prefers deleting it at a verse ending because pauses commonly omit final ya.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : قرىء { إذا يسر } بإثبات الياء ، ثم قال : وحذفها أحب إلي

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says Arabic may drop ya and rely on the preceding kasra, citing a poetic example.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء : والعرب قد تحذف الياء وتكتفي بكسرة ما قبلها ، وأنشد

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali explains omission at pauses and rhyme: pauses alter sounds, so letters resembling additions can be deleted; readers retaining ya argue that final ya remains in verbs.
rows.anchor: الفواصل والقوافي موضع وقف والوقف موضع تغيير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hajr means intellect because it restrains wrongdoing; related terms for reason and understanding also imply restraint or keeping count.
rows.anchor: الحجر العقل سمي به لأنه يمنع عن الوقوع فيما لا ينبغي

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says a person with hajr masters and controls himself; reason is named for preventing vice, with a stone-root also suggesting restraint.
rows.anchor: والعرب تقول إنه لذو حجر إذا كان قاهرا لنفسه ضابطا لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question whether this is an oath for a person of reason rhetorically intensifies the point: a discerning person sees signs of divine unity and lordship in these objects.
rows.anchor: استفهام والمراد منه التأكيد كمن ذكر حجة باهرة

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qadi argues the oath must actually be by the Lord of these things, since the verse intensifies the oath and a rational person may not swear by created objects.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي : وهذه الآية تدل على ما قلنا : أن القسم واقع برب هذه الأمور

rows.speaker: أبي حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa holds freeing a slave to be the best form of charity; this verse's placing emancipation before feeding supports him.
rows.anchor: عند أبي حنيفة العتق أفضل أنواع الصدقات

rows.speaker: صاحبيه
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa's two companions hold that charity is better than emancipation.
rows.anchor: وعند صاحبيه الصدقة أفضل

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari derives masghaba from hunger, maqraba from kinship or closeness, and matraba from becoming poor and stuck to earth; atraba means becoming wealthy like earth in abundance.
rows.anchor: المسغبة والمقربة والمتربة مفعلات من سغب إذا جاع

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi calls matraba a verbal noun meaning becoming so poor one clings to the dust.
rows.anchor: المتربة مصدر من قولهم ترب يترب تربا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan explains a day of hunger as a day on which people are eager for food; Arabic similarly calls a night 'sleeping' or a day 'fasting.'
rows.anchor: ما قاله الحسن : وهو نائم يوم محروص فيه على الطعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spending during famine and necessity is harder for the soul and earns greater reward, as in 2:177 and 76:8.
rows.anchor: إخراج المال في وقت القحط والضرورة أثقل على النفس وأوجب للأجر

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reads dhā masghaba in the accusative as an adjective of the day: feeding on a day characterized by hunger.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن : ( ذا مسغبة ) نصبه بإطعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person of dust-poverty is so destitute that there is nothing above to shelter him or beneath to cushion him.
rows.anchor: مسكينا قد لصق بالتراب من فقره وضره

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas saw a poor person lying on the ground and identified him as the person meant by 'dust-poor.'
rows.anchor: روى أن ابن عباس مر بمسكين لاصق بالتراب

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafiʿi argues that a miskin can own something: otherwise qualifying him as dust-poor would redundantly repeat that he owns nothing.
rows.anchor: واحتج الشافعي بهذه الآية على أن المسكين قد يكون بحيث يملك شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who passed the difficult ascent must also belong to the believers; without faith, none of these acts benefits its doer.
rows.anchor: فإنه إن لم يكن منهم لم ينتفع بشيء من هذه الطاعات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The delayed mention of faith may be rhetorical rather than chronological, as in a poem that mentions a father's and grandfather's status after the son's.
rows.anchor: أن هذا التراخي في الذكر لا في الوجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, faith must be the person's final state at death, since dying in faith is required for reward from earlier obedience.
rows.anchor: أن يكون المراد ، ثم كان في عاقبة أمره من الذين آمنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third view allows reward for good deeds done before conversion if the person later accepts Muhammad; Hakim ibn Hizam asked about his pre-Islamic good works and the Prophet replied that he entered Islam with them.
rows.anchor: أن حكيم بن حزام بعدما أسلم قال لرسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth reading delays faith in rank, not time: its reward greatly exceeds freeing a slave or giving charity.
rows.anchor: تراخي الإيمان وتباعده في الرتبة والفضيلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mutual exhortation to patience means steadfastness in faith, obedience, avoiding sins and enduring trials.
rows.anchor: الصبر على الإيمان والثبات عليه أو الصبر على المعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mutual exhortation to mercy means helping the oppressed and poor and restraining a person approaching wrongdoing; it requires directing others toward truth and away from evil.
rows.anchor: على أن يرحم المظلوم أو الفقير ، أو يرحم المقدم على منكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These believers are the leading Companions, including the four caliphs, distinguished by endurance in religion and compassion for people.
rows.anchor: وهذه الطائفة هم أكابر الصحابة كالخلفاء الأربعة وغيرهم

rows.speaker: بعض المحققين
rows.claim: A learned authority sums up religious conduct as two foundations: truthfulness toward God and good character toward people.
rows.anchor: إن الأصل في التوصف أمران : صدق مع الحق ؟ وخلق مع الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those believers are identified at the Resurrection as the companions of the right.
rows.anchor: ثم إنه سبحانه لما وصف هؤلاء المؤمنين بين أنهم من هم في القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura urges obedience and warns against disobedience; oaths by beneficial created things prompt reflection and gratitude because divine oaths weigh heavily on the heart.
rows.anchor: المقصود من هذه السورة الترغيب في الطاعات والتحذير من المعاصي

rows.speaker: جماعة من أهل الأصول
rows.claim: Some legal theorists supply 'Lord of' before the sun and other oath objects, understanding the oath to be by their Lord.
rows.anchor: التقدير ورب الشمس ورب سائر ما ذكره إلى تمام القسم

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qadi denies that 'what made it' refers to God: the oath cannot put another beside God's own oath, and the phrase should mean the heaven and its building; al-Zamakhshari objects that this disrupts the syntax with 'inspired it.'
rows.anchor: وهو أن { ما } مع ما بعده في حكم المصدر

rows.speaker: القراء
rows.claim: Readers vary between imala and full pronunciation in this sura's verse endings, sometimes applying imala throughout and sometimes only selectively.
rows.anchor: القراء مختلفون في فواصل هذه السورة وما أشبهها

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra explains imala in endings with roots from waw by their resemblance to words beginning with ya; forms such as tala and daha can shift toward ya in verbs.
rows.anchor: فلما حصلت هذه الموافقة استجازوا إمالته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Full non-imala is also sound because many Arabs do not incline these alifs toward ya, and letters that historically shifted from waw or ya do not always reveal the shift in pronunciation.
rows.anchor: أن كثيرا من العرب لا يميلون هذه الألفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamza's mixed approach is also good: only alifs derived from ya warrant imala, while tala, daha and similar forms derive from waw.
rows.anchor: وأما إمالة البعض وترك إمال البعض ، كما فعله حمزة فحسن أيضا

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Seven things are sworn by through 'successful indeed' as the oath's answer; al-Zajjaj says the lām of laqad is omitted because the long passage substitutes for it.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : المعنى لقد أفلح ، لكن اللام حذفت لأن الكلام طال

rows.speaker: مجاهد والكلبي
rows.claim: Mujahid and al-Kalbi explain the sun's duha as its light.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد والكلبي : ضوؤها

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada takes duha as the whole day, an interpretation preferred by al-Farra and Ibn Qutayba.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة : هو النهار كله ، وهو اختيار الفراء وابن قتيبة

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil interprets duha as the sun's heat; Razi considers this the weakest view because heat and light accompany one another.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل : هو حر الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath highlights the sun's benefits: sunrise awakens the world as if reviving the dead, and the growing life of day culminates at noon, analogous to the people of Paradise settling in their home.
rows.anchor: فلما ظهر أثر الصبح في المشرق صار ذلك كالصور الذي ينفخ قوة الحياة

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: The moon follows the sun by remaining visible after its setting in the first half of the lunar month.
rows.anchor: وهو قول عطاء عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: قتادة والكلبي
rows.claim: Qatada and al-Kalbi say the moon follows the sun by setting after it on the new moon night.
rows.anchor: وهو قول قتادة والكلبي

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra understands following as taking light from the sun.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء : المراد من هذا التلو هو أن القمر يأخذ الضوء من الشمس

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the moon follows the sun when it becomes full and nearly matches its brightness on the white nights.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : تلاها حين استدار وكمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further view says the moon follows in apparent size and its relation to worldly interests, with a special astronomical affinity to the sun.
rows.anchor: أنه يتلوها في كبر الجرم بحسب الحس

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj makes the pronoun in 'reveals it' refer to the sun: daylight is the sun's light, and the strength of the effect indicates the strength of its cause.
rows.anchor: أنه عائد إلى الشمس وذلك لأن النهار عبارة عن نور الشمس

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Most commentators take the pronoun to refer to darkness, the world or the earth, despite no explicit prior mention, as in ordinary Arabic usage.
rows.anchor: الثاني : وهو قول الجمهور أنه عائد إلى الظلمة ، أو إلى الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night covers the sun and removes its light; this strengthens the reading that daytime reveals the sun by contrast, and the nearby pronouns then consistently refer to the sun.
rows.anchor: يعني يغشى الليل الشمس فيزيل ضوءها

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffal says all four oaths are really about the sun through its midday light, the moon's borrowing its light, its emergence in daytime and its concealment at night.
rows.anchor: وهذه الأقسام الأربعة ليست إلا بالشمس في الحقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reflecting on the sun's finite size and composite parts reveals its createdness and leads the mind to the Creator's greatness.
rows.anchor: انتقل منه إلى عظمة خالقها ، فسبحانه ما أعظم شأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night shelters animals, stills creatures and brings restorative sleep; day removes darkness and sets people, birds and other creatures moving for livelihood. Their alternation serves both work and rest, as 25:62 and 14:33 say.
rows.anchor: لكن المصلحة كانت في تعاقبهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted object of 'covers' may be the sun, the day, or anything concealed by darkness, as in 91:4, 13:3 and 113:3.
rows.anchor: فهو إما الشمس من قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Day appears when night darkness departs, or when the sun rises and becomes visible.
rows.anchor: أي ظهر بزوال ظلمة الليل ، أو ظهر وانكشف بطلوع الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath's answer says human deeds differ greatly in consequence: some lead to guidance and Paradise, others to error and Hell; the verse resembles contrasts in 59:20, 32:18 and 45:21.
rows.anchor: أعمال عباده لشتى أي مختلفة في الجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shatta is the plural of shatit and conveys separation or distance between unlike things.
rows.anchor: وشتى جمع شتيت مثل مرضى ومريض

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Commentators report that the verse was revealed about Abu Bakr and Abu Sufyan.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون : نزلت هذه الآية في أبي بكر وأبي سفيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage explains that the differing human paths end in praiseworthy or blameworthy outcomes, reward or punishment.
rows.anchor: بين معنى اختلاف الأعمال فيما قلناه من العاقبة المحمودة والمذمومة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Giving may mean spending wealth in every good cause, including freeing slaves, ransoming captives and supporting Muslims, whether obligatory or voluntary, as in 8:3, 76:8 and 92:17-20.
rows.anchor: إنفاق المال في جميع وجوه الخير من عتق الرقاب وفك الأسارى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, giving includes fulfilling both financial rights and the self's duties of obedience to God.
rows.anchor: يتناول إعطاء حقوق المال وإعطاء حقوق النفس في طاعة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taqwa means avoiding everything improper; whether it requires avoiding minor sins was discussed under 2:2.
rows.anchor: فهو إشارة إلى الاحتراز عن كل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One meaning of al-husna is the testimony of God's unity, encompassing tawhid and prophethood; giving and restraint alone do not benefit without faith, as in 90:14-17.
rows.anchor: أنها قول لا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another meaning is belief in the goodness of God's prescribed bodily and financial laws.
rows.anchor: أن الحسنى عبارة عما فرضه الله تعالى من العبادات على الأبدان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third meaning is confidence that God will replace what is spent, as promised in 34:39 and illustrated by 2:261; denying this promise reflects bad opinion of God.
rows.anchor: أن الحسنى هو الخلف الذي وعده الله في قوله : { وما أنفقتم من شيء فهو يخلفه }

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء
rows.claim: Abu al-Darda reports that two angels call daily for God to replace the spender's wealth and destroy the miser's.
rows.anchor: وروي عن أبي الدرداء أنه قال : ( ما من يوم غربت فيه الشمس

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Al-Husna can mean reward or Paradise; Qatada says the person believes God's promise and acts for it.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة : صدق بموعود الله فعمل لذلك الموعود

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffal says the word broadly includes every good quality, as in 9:52 and 42:23; increased reward is also called good in 42:23 and 41:50.
rows.anchor: قال القفال : وبالجملة أن الحسنى لفظة تسع كل خصلة حسنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-yusra can mean Paradise, goodness, ease in all required acts and omissions, or renewed return to obedience; al-usra can mean shirk, hardship, or returning to withholding financial rights. Al-Qaffal explains both by their outcomes: obedience yields ease and sin hardship.
rows.anchor: فكل ما أدت عاقبته إلى يسر وراحة وأمور محمودة ، فإن ذلك من اليسرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine ending may refer to a group of deeds, a feminine noun such as khilla or faʿla, the return to a prior act, or a feminine 'way'; it may also call Paradise easy because its promise makes difficult worship feel easy.
rows.anchor: أن المراد من اليسرى والعسرى إن كان جماعة الأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If yusra means Paradise, making it easy means granting honored entry, as 13:23-24, 39:73 and 13:24 describe.
rows.anchor: بإدخال الله تعالى إياهم في الجنة بسهولة وإكرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If yusra means good deeds, ease means energizing the person to perform them without the sluggishness of hypocrites, as 2:45, 4:142 and 9:38 illustrate.
rows.anchor: هو تسهيلها على من أراد حتى لا يعتريه من التثاقل
